subject.title: [Feature]: Discord thread-reply mention gate — respond to thread starter freely, require mention for follow-up replies

question: Should Discord expose a distinct opt-in autoThread follow-up mention policy, separate from the ordinary parent-channel versus thread requireMention override?
rationale: The requested behavior adds public Discord config surface and changes which thread messages reach the agent, so code inspection can prove the gap but cannot choose the permanent API or default semantics safely.

options.title: Add a distinct opt-in follow-up gate
options.body: Add a Discord-owned, default-off config such as an autoThread follow-up mention gate that preserves current behavior unless explicitly enabled.

options.title: Fold it into thread.requireMention
options.body: Use one nested thread requireMention override for both ordinary threads and bot-owned autoThreads, accepting a broader API contract and migration/documentation burden.

options.title: Defer to broader strict mention mode
options.body: Keep this issue open until maintainers choose a cross-channel strict implicit-mention design instead of a Discord-specific config key.

recommendation.title: Add a distinct opt-in follow-up gate
recommendation.body: Add a Discord-owned, default-off config such as an autoThread follow-up mention gate that preserves current behavior unless explicitly enabled.

likelyOwner.reason: The central mention-policy refactor and issue timeline both point to steipete as the strongest routing candidate for the product/API decision.
